title: Water Heater Repair & Replacement | Harbourview Plumbing
description: Tank and tankless water heater repair, flushing and same-day replacement in Port Alder, Cedar Falls and Millbrook, with a water test first.
lead: No hot water usually means one failed part, not a whole new heater. We test first, repair what can be repaired, and replace only when the tank itself is done.

sections.heading: Hard water is the real problem in the valley
sections.html:
Wells in Cedar Falls and Millbrook commonly run hard and high in iron. In a tank heater that turns into a layer of scale on the bottom that the burner or element has to heat through, which is the popping and rumbling sound people describe. In a tankless unit it coats the heat exchanger until the unit throws an error and shuts down.

On the harbour side, the water is softer, so tanks tend to fail from age and anode wear instead. Either way, a ten-minute water test tells us which situation you're in, and that decides whether a flush, a part or a new heater makes sense.

sections.heading: Repairs we carry parts for
items: Elements and thermostats for electric tanks
Thermocouples, thermopiles and gas valves for atmospheric gas tanks
Igniters and flame sensors for power-vented tanks
Anode rods, including powered anodes for smelly hot water
Descaling kits and isolation valves for tankless units

sections.heading: When we recommend replacing
sections.html: If the tank is leaking from the body, it can't be repaired and we'll say so plainly. If it's over twelve years old and needs a gas valve, the repair may cost close to half a new heater, so we'll show you both prices. When you do replace, we size the new unit to your household and your water, and we install a mixing valve and expansion tank where code calls for them.

sections.heading: Typical prices
sections.note_html: Example prices. Your plumber confirms the price before starting.

items.q: Can you replace it the same day?
items.a: Usually, yes. We keep the common 40 and 50 gallon gas and electric tanks in stock, so a morning call is normally hot water by the afternoon.
It can be for larger households with steady demand, but on hard well water it needs a softener or regular descaling. We'll give you the running cost of both options for your home.
